questions.question: How many Grand Slam tournaments are played in a year in tennis?
questions.questionHtml: How many Grand Slam tournaments are played in a year in tennis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 4.

Important Points

  • The four annual tennis tournaments, also known as majors, are collectively called the Grand Slam.
  • The ITF—the International Tennis Federation—operates the Grand Slam.
  • The Grand Slam tournaments consist of the mid-January Australian Open, the late May French Open or Roland Garros, the Wimbledon at the end of June and the US Open at the end of August.
  • The four Grand Slam tennis tournaments are played over the course of 2 weeks.
  • The oldest is Wimbledon Tennis, established in 1877, then comes the US Open in 1881 followed by the French Open in 1891, and the last is Australian Open in 1905.
  • The Australian tennis and US tournaments are played on hard courts, the French Open on clay courts, and the Wimbledon on grass courts.
  • Before 1924-1925, the French Open tournament was not considered a Grand Slam.
  • Together, the four majors are considered a "boxed set" of Grand Slam tournaments in all three disciplines (singles, doubles, and mixed doubles).
  • During the course of a lifetime, winning all four majors is considered a career Grand Slam.
  • It is considered a non-calendar year Grand Slam to win the four majors in consecutive events, but not in the same year.

questions.question: Which of the following is the first grand slam of the year?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the first grand slam of the year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Australian Open.

Key Points

  • The Australian Open is the first Grand Slam tournament of the tennis calendar year.
  • It is held annually in Melbourne, Australia, during the last fortnight of January.
  • The tournament features men's and women's singles, doubles, mixed doubles, and junior championships.
  • The Australian Open was first held in 1905 and has been played at Melbourne Park since 1988.
  • The tournament's surface is hardcourt, specifically Plexicushion, which replaced Rebound Ace in 2008.

Additional Information

  • Grand Slam Tournaments
    • There are four major Grand Slam tournaments: Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, and US Open.
    • Each tournament is held annually and features the best tennis players from around the world.
    • Winning all four Grand Slam titles in a single year is known as a "Calendar Grand Slam."
    • The Grand Slam tournaments are the most prestigious events in the sport of tennis, offering the highest ranking points, prize money, and media attention.
  • Australian Open History
    • The Australian Open was originally known as the Australasian Championships and later the Australian Championships before becoming the Australian Open in 1969.
    • It was initially played on grass courts before switching to hardcourt surfaces.
    • Notable players like Novak Djokovic, Roger Federer, and Serena Williams have multiple Australian Open titles.
  • Melbourne Park
    • Melbourne Park is the venue for the Australian Open and features state-of-the-art facilities.
    • The complex includes the Rod Laver Arena, which is the main stadium with a retractable roof.
    • Melbourne Park also hosts various entertainment and cultural events throughout the year.
  • Tennis Scoring System
    • A standard tennis match is played in a best-of-three or best-of-five sets format.
    • A player must win six games to win a set, with a margin of at least two games.
    • If the score reaches 6-6 in games, a tiebreak is played to determine the set winner.
    • The first player to win four points in a game, with a margin of two points, wins the game.

  • She is the first Olympic medal-winning Indian badminton player, the first Indian to reach the final of the BWF World Championship, and the only Indian to win the BWF or Junior World Championships.
  • She became the first Indian female to win a 4-star tournament in 2006 and the youngest Asian.
  • She became the first Indian to win two Commonwealth Games singles gold medals (2010 and 2018).​

Additional Information

  • Prakash Padukone is a former Indian badminton player; who was ranked World No. 1 in 1980.

questions.question: Where was the Durand Cup Tournament started in India in 1888?
questions.questionHtml: Where was the Durand Cup Tournament started in India in 1888?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Shimla.

Key Points

  • The Durand Cup is one of the oldest football tournaments in the world and the oldest in Asia.
  • It was started in the year 1888 in Shimla, India.
  • The tournament was initially a military affair, organized by then India's Foreign Secretary, Mortimer Durand.
  • Over the years, it has grown to become a prestigious event in Indian football, with clubs from across the country participating.

Additional Information

  • History of the Durand Cup
    • The Durand Cup was named after its founder, Sir Mortimer Durand, who established the tournament to improve the physical fitness of British troops in India.
    • Initially, the tournament was restricted to the British Indian Army troops, but over time, it was opened to civilian teams as well.
    • The first edition of the Durand Cup was held in 1888 in Shimla, the summer capital of British India.
    • In 1940, the tournament was shifted to New Delhi, where it continued to be held annually until 2018. It was then moved to Kolkata in 2019.
  • Significance of the Durand Cup
    • The Durand Cup is the third oldest football tournament in the world, after the English FA Cup and the Scottish Cup.
    • It holds a special place in Indian football history and is considered a prestigious trophy for clubs across the country.
    • The tournament has witnessed participation from some of the top clubs in Indian football, including Mohun Bagan, East Bengal, and Mohammedan Sporting.
    • Winning the Durand Cup is seen as a major achievement for any club in India.
  • Format of the Tournament
    • The Durand Cup follows a knockout format, with teams competing in a series of elimination rounds to reach the final.
    • The tournament usually features a group stage followed by knockout rounds, including quarter-finals, semi-finals, and the final.
    • The winner of the Durand Cup is awarded the Durand Cup trophy, which is considered one of the most prestigious trophies in Indian football.
  • Modern Developments
    • In recent years, the Durand Cup has seen increased participation from clubs in the Indian Super League (ISL) and the I-League.
    • The tournament has also received support from the All India Football Federation (AIFF) and various state football associations.
    • Efforts have been made to modernize the tournament and increase its popularity among football fans in India.
    • The Durand Cup continues to be an important event in the Indian football calendar, attracting attention from fans and media alike.
